The GRASP2018 calculation of Bezmalinovich et al. (arXiv:2602.22886) covers Se I but prints no line-by-line data.

77Se ground-term hyperfine structure: an ESR study of gas-phase Se atoms (Chem. Phys. Lett., 1972, ScienceDirect pii 0009261472850772) reports a 77Se hyperfine constant for 4p4 3P2, but the page could not be opened (publisher blocks automated access), so no number is entered.

Kernahan and Pang, Can. J. Phys. 54, 103 (1976) (measured A of the 488.7 and 776.8 nm forbidden lines) and Ubelis and Berzinsh, Phys. Scr. 34, 805 (1986): publisher and archive copies not accessible. The electronic Table 2 of Morton 2000 (ApJS 130, 403) is not in the archived PDF that was read (text sections 7.4 and 10.4 only).
conflicts: 3S°1 lifetime: laser 2.9(5) ns (Bengtsson et al. 1992, Z. Phys. D) vs beam-foil 1.7(2) ns (Dynefors 1975); laser value kept. All A values of Ubelis and Berzinsh 1986 for the 196.1 / 204.0 / 206.3 / 241.3 nm lines (3.63, 1.67, 0.56, 0.020 e8 s^-1) are tied to 1.7 ns and are therefore 1.7x larger than the Morton 2000 values (2.13, 0.98, 0.33 e8 s^-1) kept here, whose sum equals 1/2.9 ns
5S°2 lifetime: 493(15) ns (laser, Bengtsson et al. 1992) vs 290(100) ns (Berzinsh / Ubelis estimate) vs < 89 ns (Corliss and Bozman); theory spans 440-2390 ns

Level energies: the NIST Handbook table (Lindgren and Palenius scale) puts every excited level 0.230 cm^-1 higher than NIST ASD (Morillon and Verges scale, e.g. 3S°1 50997.161 vs 50996.931); Li et al. 2021 measured 50996.89(15) and support the ASD scale used here
Ionization energy: 78658.15(5) (NIST ASD, from Li et al. 2021) vs 78658.35(12) (Lindgren and Palenius, NIST Handbook) vs 78658.12(10) cm^-1 (Morillon and Verges)
Abundances: the older NIST Handbook isotope table prints 9.2 % (76), 49.8 % (80), 8.8 % (82); the NIST Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions values (9.37, 49.61, 8.73 %) are used
notes: NIST ASD has Se I level energies but no classified lines; the E1 transitions here are the classified persistent lines of the NIST Handbook of Basic Atomic Spectroscopic Data, re-expressed with the NIST ASD level energies of data/nist/Se_I_levels.tsv (identification by configuration, term and J). The 'wavelength_nm' field gives the observed wavelength as listed (vacuum below 200 nm, air above) with its 'medium'; the wavelength in each label is the vacuum Ritz value from the NIST ASD energies. A values of the six 5s-4p4 lines are those of Morton 2000 as listed by NIST (compilation: Bengtsson et al. laser lifetimes x Ubelis and Berzinsh branching); rme_J_ea0 is derived from them (convention of SCHEMA.md). Branching fractions of the 3S°1 level are derived from the four Ubelis and Berzinsh A values; those of 5S°2 from the two Morton A values. Lifetimes of the 4p4 metastable levels and all forbidden-line rates are 1964 THEORY (Garstang); A_s of a forbidden line is the sum of the calculated M1 and E2 parts given in its note. Natural selenium is 92 % even isotopes (I = 0) and 7.6 % 77Se (I = 1/2). Second pass 2026-10-01: Bengtsson et al., Z. Phys. D 23, 29 (1992) was read directly (first two pages): tau(3S°1) = 2.9(5) ns and f_abs(196.0 nm) = 0.074(16) are confirmed. Roederer & Lawler 2012 (Table 5) recommend the Morton A values with uncertainties 213(37), 98(17), 33(6) and 1.70(10) x 10^6 s^-1 (stored as alternatives) and note that isotope shifts are small and the 77Se hyperfine structure negligible for abundance work. Morton 2000 (Sec. 7.4) states that the excited-level energies of Morillon and Verges were raised by 0.23 cm^-1 following Lindgren and Palenius, and that the beam-foil lifetime of Dynefors is 59 % of the adopted laser value.
